$ corvex gate audit --help

--- stdout ---
Audit the gates instead of what they guard.

Three numbers per gate: how long it waited for an answer, how often the answer was no, and — the sharp one — how long passed between acknowledging the required reading and deciding. A gap of exactly zero means both happened in one command, which is a keystroke rather than a review.

It reads the gate files under .corvex/runs/gates/, not the activity ledger: the ledger cannot tell a rejection from an expiry, records no duration for --approve-gates, and has no reading marks at all. Gates auto-approved by --approve-gates never appear here, because no gate file is written for them — policy approval is a declared choice, not a fast human.

Expiry is reported beside the rejection rate and never inside it: nobody showed up is not the same answer as no.

Usage:
  corvex gate audit [flags]

Flags:
      --since string             only gates opened within this window — 90m, 36h, 7d (0 for all) (default "7d")
      --repo --repo .            only gates of one repository (--repo . for the current one)
      --all                      every gate ever recorded, ignoring --since (the window a small population needs)
      --suspect-under duration   call out decisions faster than this in the printed hint (policy, never in --json) (default 10s)
      --json                     print machine-readable JSON instead of formatted output
  -h, --help                     help for audit

Global Flags:
      --no-color   Disable color output
  -q, --quiet      Suppress per-task progress; print only failures/errors and the final summary

--- stderr ---
(empty)

--- error ---
(nil)
